{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Howard Eli Haber''' (born 3 February 1952 in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York City]])<ref>{{cite book|title=American Men and Women of Science|publisher=Thomson Gale|year=2004}}</ref> is an American physicist, specializing in theoretical [[elementary particle physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://physics.aps.org/authors/howard_e_haber|title=Howard E. Haber|website=APS Physics}}</ref>

Howard Haber received in 1973 his bachelor's degree and master's degree from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) and received in 1978 his Ph.D. from the [[University of Michigan]] at [[Ann Arbor]]. He was a postdoc at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory from 1978 to 1980 and at the University of Pennsylvania from 1980 to 1982. He joined the faculty of the physics department and the University of California, Santa Cruz, where he became an associate professor in 1989 and a full professor in 1990 (continuing to the present). From 1982 to the present he has been a visiting physicist with the Theory Group at [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center|SLAC]].<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=C.V. (shorter form)|website=UCSC Homepage, Howard E. Haber|url=http://scipp.ucsc.edu/~haber/webpage/hehvitashort2.pdf}}</ref>

From 1985 to 1988 Haber held an Outstanding Junior Investigator Award from [[United States Department of Energy|DOE]]. In 1993 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. In 2009 he received a [[Humboldt Research Award]], with which he was a visiting professor at the University of Bonn.<ref name=CV/>

His research deals with the physics of the [[Higgs boson]] and also possible [[Standard Model]] extensions such as the low-energy sector of [[supersymmetry]] theory,<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Haber, Howard E.|title=Introductory Low-Energy Supersymmetry|year=1993|eprint=hep-ph/9306207 }}</ref> which he considers fundamental for the study of physics beyond the Standard Model.<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Haber, Howard E.|title=The Supersymmetric Top-Ten Lists|year=1993|eprint=hep-ph/9308209 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Haber, Howard E.|title=Anticipating the Next Discoveries in Particle Physics|pages=355–499|author2=Haskins, Laurel Stephenson|chapter=Supersymmetric Theory and Models|date=4 May 2018|arxiv=1712.05926|doi=10.1142/9789813233348_0006|isbn=978-981-323-333-1|s2cid=118857741}}</ref>

In 2017 he, together with three collaborators, received the [[Sakurai Prize]] for, according to the laudation, "instrumental contributions to the theory of the properties, reactions, and signatures of the Higgs boson".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Haber&first_nm=Howard&year=2017|title=2017 J. J. Sakurai Prize, Howard E. Haber|website=APS Physics}}</ref>
